tasks.short: Document methods and write technical reports

steps.what: Document methods used and select verified information for the technical report
Write a technical report describing methods and collected information

loop.purpose: Draft methods and results narrative from supplied records only.
loop.input: Checked report source pack with source versions, method parameters, verified results and limitations.
loop.output: Report draft with each factual statement linked to its source record.
loop.check: Technician checks every methods statement, number and limitation against the actual processing records and verifies that wording does not imply unsupported accuracy or causality.
loop.stop: At most two redrafts; unsupported statements or unclear methods are written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can place tables but cannot compose a faithful account of varied methods and limitations.

steps.what: Verify technical meaning and approve the complete report version for internal use

tasks.design: Use a native template in {DOCS} for report structure and a bounded drafting loop for the methods narrative. The technician supplies checked records, verifies every generated claim and approves the complete internal report; underlying analysis remains separate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report prose must accurately connect varied methods, results and limitations.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can turn selected records into a first narrative while retaining source links.
tasks.still_hard: Explain methodological limitations and avoid overstating what the imagery establishes.
tasks.human_edge: Know whether the report faithfully describes the work actually performed.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft writing where records are usable; scientific responsibility stays unchanged.

reach.learn: State uncertainty and distinguish measured results from interpretation.

evidence.claim: Novo Nordisk's NovoScribe case describes report-writing assistance with human approval; it is an adjacent vendor case, not evidence of a remote-sensing time-saving rate.
The remote-sensing report design and savings are unmeasured model-knowledge scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is methods documentation and report writing, excluding acquisition, processing, analysis and external publication.

Existing processing owners produce logs and verified results before s1. The technician captures dataset and result versions, method sequence, parameter values, units, limitations and source references during retained s1 time; no free structured methods account is assumed.
The loop uses only s1's source pack. Missing or contradictory records require manual reconstruction in retained human time; no automated extraction saving is claimed.
Test native templates first. Draft checking in s2 is additional to unchanged final whole-report review in s3. Additional focal upkeep is 6 hours per 100 baseline hours.
research_questions: Does a checked draft accurately preserve methodological limitations without increasing final review time?

already_counted.description: Source pack preparation and methods capture remain.
Draft meaning checks remain within the writing step.
Final scientific review and approval remain.

incremental.description: Maintain drafting instructions and investigate source-link failures.

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete report version and bound source-pack versions checked in s3; any content, figure or source change voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+35*0.65+30=87.75; gross=12.25, upkeep=6, central net=6.25. Conservative 0-4 allows extensive rewriting for unusual methods; source preparation and final review retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Specify specialized software routines needed to customize and integrate image analysis
Develop computer software routines implementing the specified image-analysis behaviour

loop.purpose: Draft a bounded image-processing routine for review.
loop.input: Routine specification, interface versions, reference examples and independently stated expected results.
loop.output: Code candidate and explanation of transformations.
loop.check: Technician reads the code for coordinate, unit, no-data and resampling semantics and compares it with the independently defined expected results; successful execution alone is insufficient.
loop.stop: At most two revisions; unexplained transformations or unresolved errors go to manual implementation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native processing tools are tried first; bespoke interface and algorithm glue requires code rather than a fixed template.

steps.what: Test scientific correctness and approve the exact software routine for internal use

tasks.design: Try native processing configuration in the {OTHER} geospatial development environment before writing bespoke code. For remaining custom routines, use a bounded coding loop while the technician retains specification, code review, scientific testing and approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Custom integration glue takes implementation effort even when its intended behaviour is known.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded coding assistant can draft implementation against explicit interfaces and reference examples.
tasks.still_hard: Detect scientifically wrong results that run successfully and protect against changed interfaces.
tasks.human_edge: Define correct results independently of the generated implementation.
tasks.altitude: Less initial coding for suitable routines; no automatic deployment or new scientific decision right.

reach.learn: Define independent reference cases and edge-case expectations.

evidence.claim: Bounded code drafting can assist implementation against an explicit specification; the remote-sensing design and saving are unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is developing the custom routine, excluding its later repeated operational use, data acquisition and scientific method invention.

OTHER is the existing geospatial software development and test environment. The technician captures interface versions, input schemas, coordinate systems, units, no-data policy, intended operations and expected outputs during retained s1 time; no free machine-readable specification is assumed.
Existing data owners supply reference datasets before s1. The technician defines independent expected results and cases during s1 rather than accepting model-generated answers as the test oracle.
Code remains a draft until s3 checks scientific behaviour and records exact version approval. Unknown interfaces, sensitive input restrictions or failed tests require manual development.
Native configuration is tested first. Incremental focal maintenance for assistant instructions and additional dependency checks is 8 hours per 100 baseline hours beyond ordinary development testing.
research_questions: Can assisted routines pass independent spatial, unit and no-data tests with less total implementation effort?

already_counted.description: Code review and correction remain within implementation.
Scientific testing and version approval remain.

incremental.description: Maintain coding instructions and perform additional dependency checks.

approvals.approved_version: Exact code revision, dependency versions, input specification and test evidence approved in s3; any change voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+40*0.60+30=84; gross=16, upkeep=8, central net=8. Conservative 0-4 allows substantial correction and unsuitable routines returning to manual implementation; testing receives no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate on reducing farming's environmental impacts

steps.what: Collaborate with agricultural workers to apply remote sensing information to environmental improvement efforts

tasks.design: Keep practical collaboration with agricultural workers human, supported by verified maps in {DOCS}. Discuss local conditions and limitations before agreeing follow-up; no automatic farm treatment recommendation is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Remote observations need interpretation in the actual farming context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing maps can support conversation, but do not replace local knowledge.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish a useful environmental signal from a misleading proxy and agree feasible action.
tasks.human_edge: Listen to farmers' practical constraints and explain uncertainty clearly.
tasks.altitude: Collaboration and advisory responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss field practices and environmental effects
reach.learn: Connect map limitations with actual field observations.

evidence.claim: The NPPL trial used soil-scan task maps for variable herbicide dosing and reported lower product use; it does not measure savings in technician-farmer collaboration.

assumptions: Boundary is collaboration, excluding map production, agronomic prescription and physical farm operations.
Existing analysts produce verified sensing information before s1; agricultural workers describe current field conditions during s1. No prior structured treatment-suitability flag is assumed.

Agricultural workers' existing discussion time remains unchanged outside the focal denominator. Native document access is sufficient; no new tool, survey or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Local field conditions and advisory responsibility
research_questions: Which map limitations most affect the practical usefulness of proposed environmental improvements?

already_counted.description: All contextual discussion and clarification remains.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Map or product-use benefits do not remove collaboration time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide sensing data for environmental work

steps.what: Select appropriate remote sensing data and capture the environmental data request specification
Package selected data and provenance for the specified environmental use
Check coverage and limitations and provide the approved data to the environmental analyst

tasks.design: Configure native exports and manifests in the {OTHER} geospatial data system from a technician-checked delivery specification. The technician selects suitable data, verifies the package's actual coverage and limitations and releases its exact version to the analyst.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated manual file selection, export setup and provenance copying can slow recurring data requests.
tasks.enabler_now: Native export profiles can package specified existing data and metadata without selecting its scientific use.
tasks.still_hard: Choose temporal and spatial coverage appropriate to the environmental issue and explain uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when available observations cannot support the requested environmental analysis.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive packaging; suitability and release decisions stay with the technician.

reach.task: Use sensing data in environmental analysis
reach.learn: Specify coverage needs and understand missing observations.

evidence.claim: Copernicus supplies corrected Sentinel-2 imagery and mosaics, demonstrating available prepared source data rather than this delivery design or time-saving rate.
Native package generation from checked specifications is an unmeasured model-knowledge proposal.

assumptions: Boundary is providing existing approved data, excluding acquisition, quality verification, image integration, modelling and dust detection itself. Upstream savings are not counted again.

OTHER is geospatial data-management software. The analyst supplies the environmental purpose and desired coverage through the existing request process. The technician clarifies and captures recipient, dataset identifiers and versions, extent, time range, variables, format, units, access permission and limitations during retained s1 time.

Existing data owners supply source files and provenance before s1. s2 uses s1's checked specification and source versions; uncertain rights or incomplete metadata require manual handling without packaging saving.
s3 checks actual coverage, units, no-data handling and manifest meaning before release. No automatic scientific suitability or environmental-risk flag is presumed.

Test native exports first. Existing export runtime earns no saving; only currently repeated human packaging setup and metadata copying are changed. Additional focal upkeep is 8 hours per 100 baseline hours.
unknowns: Recurring request formats and existing export profiles
research_questions: Can native profiles reproduce complete data packages with correct provenance and coverage while reducing manual setup?

already_counted.description: Request clarification, specification capture and release verification remain.

incremental.description: Maintain export profiles and resolve additional packaging exceptions.

approvals.approved_version: Exact package and manifest versions, source datasets, coverage, limitations and recipient approved before release in s3; any change voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+0+25=60; gross=40, focal upkeep=8, central net=32. Conservative 6-18 allows bespoke requests and incomplete metadata; suitability selection and release review keep all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician retains scientific meaning, code validation and data-release decisions while drafts and recurring packages may take less clerical effort.
reach: Define independent scientific test cases with remote sensing scientists.
Clarify useful environmental data coverage with analysts.
role.ambitious_version: Use any released drafting and packaging time to resolve data limitations with the people applying the results.
